issues.description: The interface for the ride capability is named inconsistently across artifacts. The problem statement UML and the template Main.java refer to an interface named 'Rideable' (declared in problem_statement.md and used in the commented example in Main.java). The solution implementation, however, defines an interface named 'Mountable' (src/de/tum/cit/ase/Mountable.java) and the classes Pig and Seal implement Mountable (Pig.java implements Mountable at line 3; Seal.java implements Mountable at line 4). The solution also contains an (effectively) empty Rideable.java file. This identifier mismatch (Rideable vs Mountable) will confuse students which interface name to implement and may cause compilation or test mismatches when template/tests expect 'Rideable' but solution/tests or reference implementations use 'Mountable'.
issues.suggestedFix: Make the interface name consistent across all artifacts. Preferred fixes: (a) Rename the solution's Mountable.java to Rideable.java and update Pig.java and Seal.java to implement Rideable (remove the empty Rideable.java file), or (b) Update the problem statement UML and the template Main.java to refer to 'Mountable' instead of 'Rideable'. Ensure the chosen name is used in the interface file and by all implementing classes and in the template/test code so students have one unambiguous identifier to implement.
